prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses on loans is an expense we incur to maintain an allowance for credit losses at a level that management deems appropriate to absorb expected losses on existing loans in accordance with GAAP. For a description of the factors taken into account by our management in determining the allowance for credit losses see “—Financial Condition—Allowance for Credit Losses.”

The macro economic environment is continuously changing, primarily due to the pace of economic growth, inflation, changing interest rates, global trade tensions, tariffs, unemployment, global unrest, the war in Ukraine, conflicts in the Middle East, political uncertainty, natural disasters and trade issues that may impact the provision and therefore the allowance. Gross loans, excluding loans held for sale, totaled $4.19 billion at September 30, 2026. The allowance for credit losses as a percentage of loans was 4.97% at September 30, 2026, compared to 4.69% at September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Generally, noninterest expense is composed of all employee expenses and costs associated with operating our facilities, obtaining and retaining customer relationships and providing bank services. The largest components of noninterest expense are a credit enhancement receivable valuation adjustment, BaaS loan and fraud expense combined, salaries and employee benefits and data processing and software licenses. Noninterest expense also includes operational expenses, such as legal and professional expenses, occupancy, point of sale expenses, FDIC assessments, director and staff expenses, excise taxes, marketing and other expenses.

Comparison of the quarter ended September 30, 2026 to the comparable quarter in the prior year

The $14.7 million increase in noninterest expenses for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to a $3.8 million increase in legal and professional expenses, $2.3 million increase in data processing and software licenses and a $1.9 million increase in salary and employee benefits. These increases are largely due to the growth of the Company and investments in technology and risk management. BaaS loan expense increased $2.9 million, which is related to increased CCBX loan activity, and BaaS fraud expense increased $2.0 million, however that expense is offset by the increase in BaaS fraud income.

tax.text: The amount of income tax expense we incur is impacted by the amounts of our pre-tax income, tax-exempt income and other nondeductible expenses. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are reflected at current income tax rates in effect for the period in which the deferred tax assets and liabilities are expected to be realized or settled. As changes in tax laws or rates are enacted, deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted through the provision for income taxes. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce our deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized. The Company is subject to various state taxes that are assessed as CCBX activities and employees expand into new states, which increases the overall tax rate used in calculating the provision for income taxes in the current and future periods.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Comparison of the quarter ended September 30, 2026 to the comparable quarter in the prior year

Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $13.8 million, or $0.89 per diluted share, compared to net income of $13.6 million, or $0.88 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net income over the comparable period in the prior year was primarily attributable to an increase of $10.4 million in net interest income, partially offset by an increase of $9.8 million in noninterest expenses excluding BaaS loan expense and BaaS fraud expense, and $3.1 million more in provision for credit losses in excess of BaaS credit enhancement income.

BaaS credit enhancement income decreased $13.6 million, primarily due to loan growth, changes in the composition of the CCBX loan portfolio and an increase in weighted average life of loans. This increase corresponds to a $10.6 million decrease in the provision for credit losses associated with expected credit losses covered under partners' credit enhancement arrangements, with the difference between the two primarily attributable one partner's expected credit losses not expected to be fully collected under that partner's indemnification arrangement.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Comparison of the quarter ended September 30, 2026 to the comparable quarter in the prior year

Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $88.3 million, compared to $77.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $10.4 million, or 13.4%. The increase in net interest income compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025 was primarily related to growth in loans receivable, partially offset by a decrease in loan yield and a decrease in interest from interest earning deposits with other banks due primarily to lower interest rates. The average balance of loans was $837.9 million higher, and average interest earning deposits with other banks was $56.4 million higher for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Total interest and fees on loans were $113.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $100.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $12.7 million increase in interest and fees on loans for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, was largely due to growth in loans, primarily from CCBX. Total loans receivable was $4.19 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $3.70 billion at September 30, 2025.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Our primary sources of recurring noninterest income are BaaS indemnification income, BaaS program income and service charges and fees. Noninterest income does not include loan origination fees, which are generally recognized over the life of the related loan as an adjustment to yield using the interest or similar method.

Comparison of the quarter ended September 30, 2026 to the comparable quarter in the prior year

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest income totaled $61.0 million, a decrease of $5.7 million, or 8.6%, compared to $66.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is primarily attributed to lower BaaS indemnification income, which is related to the provision for credit losses on CCBX loans as well as $3.1 million lower credit enhancement income recognized attributable one partner's expected credit losses not expected to be fully collected under that partner's indemnification arrangement. A $6.3 million increase in BaaS program income partially offset the decrease in BaaS indemnification income.

intro.text: Coastal Financial Corporation (“Company”) is a registered bank holding company, whose wholly owned subsidiaries are Coastal Community Bank (“Bank”) and Arlington Olympic LLC (“LLC”). The Company is a Washington state corporation that was organized in 2003. The Bank was incorporated and commenced operations in 1997 and is a Washington state-chartered commercial bank and Federal Reserve System (“Federal Reserve”) member bank. The LLC was formed in 2019 and owns the Company’s Arlington branch, which the Bank leases from the LLC. Our executive offices are located at 5415 Evergreen Way, Everett, Washington 98203, and our telephone number is (425) 257-9000. Our website addresses are www.coastalbank.com and www.ccbx.com. Information on our website should not be considered a part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
